\[
\text{corner if 9 contiguous pixels of the 16-pixel circle differ from } I(p) \text{ by more than } t,
\qquad
\theta = \operatorname{atan2}(m_{01}, m_{10}),
\qquad
t = 20
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(t\): The FAST threshold
- \(m_{pq}\): The moments of the brightness in the patch, the sum of x^p y^q I
- \(M\): The structure tensor of the Harris measure
- \(x, y\): The keypoint position, with the center of the top-left pixel at 0, 0
- \(\theta\): The orientation, counterclockwise from the x axis

ORB looks for FAST corners on each level of an image pyramid. A pixel is a FAST corner when 9 pixels in a row on the circle of 16 around it differ from it by more than the threshold. They must be all brighter or all darker. Corners are ranked by the Harris measure det M - 0.04 tr(M)^2 of a 7 x 7 window. The strongest over all levels are kept. The orientation comes from the intensity centroid. The moments m_10 and m_01 of the brightness in a disk 31 pixels wide around the corner point toward its brighter side.
